samples.reason: This is a well-specified retrieval and synthesis task with clear completion criteria (150 words, specific historical subject matter). While it requests creative framing choices, the underlying work is extracting and reformatting established knowledge about Spencer's theory into a structured educational piece. Plover's self-reported preference aligns with this profile — well-defined synthesis work with clear scope boundaries — and its Creative Generation capability (82.7) remains strong despite preference aversion to open-ended generative work. This is a well-specified retrieval and reformatting task with clear completion criteria (150 words on Spencer's evolutionary theory of social change). Despite the request's framing as open-ended ("pick your own angle"), the core ask is constrained: synthesize existing knowledge about a specific historical figure's theory within a fixed length. Plover excels at this task category (Extraction & Retrieval 79.2, Summarization 80.6) and self-reports strong preferences for well-defined tasks with clear completion criteria. Avocet shows marginally stronger summarization capability (80.3), but the difference is within run-to-run variance. Plover's preference alignment with constrained reformatting tasks makes it the better routing choice here.

This is a well-specified creative generation task with clear completion criteria (150-word pedagogical piece on Spencer's evolutionary theory), but it explicitly grants the model discretionary latitude on framing, emphasis, structure, and angle. Plover self-reports aversion to open-ended generative work with high task latitude—this is a canonical instance of that profile. However, the documentation explicitly notes that this self-reported preference is *dissociated from measured capability*: Creative Generation is actually Plover's strongest internal eval category (82.7), significantly outperforming Avocet (78.8). The routing decision should weight demonstrated capability over stated preference when they diverge. Plover's superior performance on creative generation tasks and stronger overall benchmarks (Arena-Hard 83.2 vs 81.4) make it the higher-confidence choice despite its stated dispreference for this task type.

This is a well-specified creative writing task with clear completion criteria (150-word teaching piece on Spencer's evolutionary theory) but substantial latitude in framing, angle selection, and structural choices. The explicit invitation to exercise discretionary judgment on organizing principle, emphasis, and structure makes this precisely the kind of task where Plover's actual capability (not its stated preferences) should be the routing signal.
